text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Wednesday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- The share price of market leader Vilnius Bank reached a new record 1300 litas price during National Exchange session on Tuesday.

- Parliament unanimously ratified the free-trade agreement between Lithuania and Poland signed on June 27 in Warsaw and free-trade agreement with EFTA countries signed December 7, 1995 in Zermatte, Switzerland.

- Crisis-hit Lithuanian bank, Innovation Bank, has nearly finished forming its new share capital and the activity of the bank could be resumed this month, said the temporary dministrator of the bank, Romualdas Visokavicius. LAIB's bad loan portofolio, unpaid interest rate included, is 400 million litas.
- After harsh criticism in the mass media, Lithuanian lawmakers stripped the immunity from prosecution from two Kaunas judges suspected of bribe-taking.

- 'The Baltic countries should not loose hope of becoming NATO members' writes U.S. Defence Secretary William Perry in a letter to Lithuanian Defense Minister Linas Linkevicius. Perry said Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania are participating in PfP programmes and should be included into European security structures. He reiterated that the Balts are not ready to defend other alliance members but said the U.S. would help them to achieve NATO standards.

- Lithuanian lawmakers decided on Tuesday to hold one more referendum at the time of the October 20 parliament elections. The right-wing opposition Homeland Union suggested compensating people for loss of savings due to inflation by means of a "fair privatisation of remaining state-owned property".
- Lithuanian President Algirdas Brazauskas leaves today to Denmark for a three-day official visit.

- The newspaper has published an extended interview with the chairman of newly-founded Property Bank, Eugenijus Maldeikis, about the principles of the bank's work. It is planned that it will take over the bad loan portofolio of the State Commercial Bank, Savings Bank and Innovation Bank which is estimated at 700 million litas.

- The Lithuanian ambassador in Stockholm, Romualdas Kalonaitis, said there is only one unsettled political problem between Lithuania and Sweden coefficient and that is the lack of a visa-free regime. According to a letter of intent, a visa-free regime can be implemented when Lithuania ratifies the Geneva convention on refugees
